assets.statement: Parity lemma refuted by Kummer: k&(n−k)=0 gives odd C(n,k); (7,3)=35 with lpf 5>7/2, and infinitely many (2^m−1,k) instances; branch-A close must instead bound small prime factors of odd coefficients directly.

L1-as-branch-B-evidence fails: Maynard bound is subsequence-only (hidden-subsequence attack) and does not match the quantifier reversal of o(log N) (needs all-N failure at positive density, not infinitely many N); repair = uniform c·log N lower bound on the full primes, an equivalent-strength open p

L1 covers only prime n-1; composite n-1 uncovered with witness n=5: 4!=3!·2!·2! in-range, so full-range finiteness is unproven — repair must bound the composite n-1 range or refile as subfamily theorem.

Counterexample n=10: k<p(m)≤√m forces odd k∈{1,3}, giving m=11,13 both prime, so no composite m exists; failure is finite-scale and does not settle the canonical asymptotic claim, whose even-n core remains without any proved supporting lemma.

Sylvester gives a prime factor >k (gpf lower bound), opposite direction to the lpf upper bound; all-factors->max(n/k,k) case satisfies Sylvester yet violates the target, so the step is vacuous at every parameter and any repair is equivalent-strength to the canonical claim

Vacuous subset fact, coprimality and both target sums never used; quantifier slip (∃-level fact offered for ∀-level proposition) and circularity confirmed; route R005 has no standing reduction and must produce a genuine bound or separating family.
